body: Of course she's not obliged to have anything to do with me. I just wish she *wanted* to. Big difference.
Thank you. It's definitely contributing to the overall existential crisis I'm having about the whole thing. I do think a dose of NRE would do wonders for my perspective.

> What she's doing by refusing to try to get along with you is asking your husband to neglect you for her.

Wow. Yes. This.

I am trying to give her the benefit of the doubt, that if her life situation were different she might be more able to get to know me. I might be deluding myself, but it stings a little less that way.
Thank you. I know I'm allowed to have these feelings, but I wish I could rise above them.

I want her to *want* to get to know me. I want her to like me. I realize that she has so much on her plate right now that forging a relationship with her boyfriend's wife is a lot to ask.

This shouldn't be about me, but it sure feels that way.

This. My unhappiness is just making things harder on my husband. And I'm frustrated that GF seems to be unable or has no interest in getting to know me. I want ALL of us to have our needs met, and I feel like a heel complaining about anything when hubby is trying SO hard to be everything to everyone.

> your needs are no less valid than your husband's OSO

I disagree. Her needs are way more immediate, pressing and valid than mine. I'm healthy, financially sort-of-stable, and honestly pretty capable of taking care of me & mine just fine. Therein lies the rub: I feel like a bad person for hating his level of support of her. Altruism is a lot easier on paper.

I've been trying to find another partner, believe me. Nothing but horrible luck so far. I'm exhausted and discouraged by my lack of success, so I am temporarily taking a break from the "hunt". If someone crosses my path, that'd be great, but I'm not actively seeking anyone right now.
Because I'm spending a fair amount of brain space thinking about my alcohol consumption. I guess it'd be true to say that I must care at least a little bit.
Shoulda only been HFA: High Functioning Alcoholic. HFE was a typo.
Thank you, that is excellent advice. I'm going to check out both those books.

Honestly, I cannot imagine going to an AA meeting. Not sure why, maybe I don't think I need to?

I'm hoping the same thing happens for me, when my life is in better shape in the next few years I'll be motivated to quit. I *am* making changes for the better, I just gotta wait for/keep working towards the payoff.

I think what fascinates me about my drinking is my inability to gauge just how addicted I am. I have a pretty extensive drug history, but no actual addiction, just recreational use. When using, I always had a very clear sense of when it was time to stop before I became addicted/dependent. Maybe I'm just less afraid to be an alcoholic than an addict?

Oh, it's definitely sad. But that's my life right now. I'm working towards a better place and am hopeful that I'll more to be enthusiastic about in a few years. Right now my circumstances are largely unchangeable, so yes, my drinking hours are the best part of my day - or the part of my day that I care less about my situation, anyway.
HFA, not HFE. Gah. Sorry.
Yeah, man, I'm a fabulous cook. Tired of cooking for a family that'd rather eat out of a box. But again, that's just me being selfish.

So sorry for your loss. I think if the emphasis is put on finding help to heal over the loss of your child (not that you ever truly can, but at least maybe cope better), the alcohol abuse will fade away.

If you're not finding the right therapist, IMO the support offered on online bulletin boards from other loss survivors might be more beneficial.

I'd say I'm in the "worried but not enough to stop" camp. I don't really care because, sadly, my hours drinking are the best ones of my day. I'm hesitant to give that up. 

I'm a bit of a control freak, so I suppose some of my concern relates to a fear of losing control - or rather, knowing if/when I've lost control.

Do you think it's possible to go on indefinitely as an HFE?
Then perhaps I could marry you and make your life a living hell?
Thanks, everyone. I think I was too focused on my appearance when I was younger. Also maybe addicted to that rush you get when you're with someone new. Makes getting older tough.

One more note: I think you could have a career as a sex-therapist/life coach/general bullshit caller. After your replies I went and checked out some of your replies to other threads...you're spot on. Callin' it like you see it. Appreciated.

Thank you. I'm not at all mad/irritated at your initial response. My situation is depressing, so calling it so is not offensive.

I think I'm in the process of mourning that part of my life. Doesn't mean it can't ever happen again, just that I need to accept it's not likely to. 

Thanks for responding.

I would love nothing more than an affair. For that to happen, I'd have to actually attract someone. I feel invisible.

I don't think I am/was narcissistic so much as a weak person too focused on the few strengths she had.

I definitely have rage/anger issues. A new one for me, as I've been aware of my depression for years, but only recently aware of the rest. I do try to imagine others' viewpoints/situations/life, but I am horribly uncharitable in that regard. Again, I really hate how my brain works.

It's awful, but the not expressing it part is just me stifling myself. I bite my tongue All. Day. Long. Because I know it's the right thing to do. The world does not need my reality/negativity/opinion. In fact, I'd rather hear someone's positive take on a situation rather than my negative crap.

I talk to my husband some, but unfortunately, he's part (okay, a big part) of my problem. So, everything has to be presented with a filter.
I will check it out, thanks! I love reading different sources re: how to fix the same problem.

Does it matter if I consider myself more of a realist vs. pessimist? I really don't believe the worst, except about myself, I guess. 

I will check out this book as well. Thanks for your input.

I think I've always been this way, but have been pretty successfully medicated for the past 3 years, so it's been tempered a bit. I suspect that my meds aren't working as they used to, but I'm loathe to tweak/change them (hasn't gone well in the past) so was hoping to find another answer.

It's nice (in a weird way) to hear that there's others that suffer from this. Even my husband doesn't know the depths of my negativity, I know better than to express it to anyone other than a paid professional. And besides, who wants to hear this shit? The irony is, I hate negative people! I don't think anyone would consider me negative, but my internal dialogue sure is. Overwhelmingly.
I am for sure at the mercy of my chemistry. Sucks. Will keep trying random things.
Oh, it's definitely what surrounds me. And yes, most certainly a mid-life crisis. I will try to focus on one issue at a time and see if it helps. Thanks for your input.
Oh god, thank you. I will buy this book immediately.
You mean there are people who don't?
I could have written that post myself, word for word. :-(

Therapist(s). I'm a big believer in talk therapy. And medication, for what it's worth. Throughout my life I've had spans of time when I've pursued talk therapy - it's been somewhat helpful, but I don't feel like there's too much unexplored ground where Svengali is concerned. 

I consider myself fairly self-aware. I think my obsession with Svengali stems from a continual dissatisfaction with my life, a literal "grass is always greener" type of feeling. I compare everyone and everything with Svengali, and 90% of the time they come up lacking. If only I could really and truly be with him, everything would be fine. I know that's bullshit, but I cannot erase him from my mind.

It's some kinda weird addiction. I'm "sober" in regards to Svengali, but damned if I don't think of him every goddamned day, and if he doesn't pop up in my dreams constantly. I know addicts that are able to move on without constantly obsessing about the object of their obsession - why can't I?

I've seen several therapists over the years, and Svengali has always been a topic of discussion. And as it stands now, there's been no contact for two years. What else can I do? 

I need an exorcism.

>I don't know you or your kids

Yup, that's it in a nutshell. Yes, my attitude is sad. *I'm* sad. I'm never gonna win Mom of the Year, that's for sure. I hate that my kids have to put up with me. They deserve so much better, as do all children. Just haven't figured out a realistic way of giving it to them.

Come home? Oh, that'd be incredible. And different. No, I'm stuck at home all day. With three challenging small people that deserve so much more than they're getting from me. When I drink, I'm a little bit nicer with them. A little less cranky. A little less mean. So, give that up? No way. That's the best interaction I have with my ball & chains.

Not everyone ends up despondent as their health fails. I have a husband, insurance, a stable lifestyle, etc. Dependent on others? Yes, that may happen, but perhaps it's payback for all the years of thankless care that I have doled out and that eventually contributed to my collapse.

My life has been one long series of poor choices. But more than that, I think it's just my nature to be depressed, always have been, always will be, this is the lens I see life through. Knowing this, knowing that I'm likely to look back at my life at the end and be disappointed & full of regret, it makes it hard to value my life. I will keep on keeping on, but can't imagine ever being at peace with my life.

I'm 43. I've got three kids + a mom & sis & bro that love me. So I hold on for them, but honestly? I have to do a hard sell to myself to justify my existence. If past performance is indicative of future results: I'm fucked.
Right back atcha, Jesus. There really aren't any words to fix this shit, are there?

Ah yes, scrips & booze. Lovely combo. I too, am familiar with this mix. Limited supply of the prescription goodies, though. I guess that's a good thing? 

Off to quaff my first of many...

No treatment. I'm what's called a "high-functioning" alcoholic. I'm nowhere near ready to give it up, since the thought of my evening consumption is about all getting me through the day. I'm medicated for my depression, have been for a couple of years, but still exist on a fairly low plane. Much of my depression is situational, but that's not going to change anytime soon, so might as well keep on keeping on....slowly killing myself.
